description: Primary sources checked for the final report. Paraphrases identify relevance and limits; literature scores are not mixed with local measurements.

records.title: ChestX-ray8: Hospital-scale Chest X-ray Database and Benchmarks on Weakly-Supervised Classification and Localization of Common Thorax Diseases
records.description: The original release describes report-derived labels for eight findings and 108,948 frontal images. Later ChestX-ray14 updates must be distinguished from that original release. Our pediatric binary dataset is different.

records.title: CheXNet: Radiologist-Level Pneumonia Detection on Chest X-Rays with Deep Learning
records.description: The reported radiologist comparison concerns pneumonia F1 on a specific test and annotation setup. It motivates a DenseNet baseline but does not establish universal clinical superiority or validate our models.

records.title: CheXpert: A Large Chest Radiograph Dataset with Uncertainty Labels and Expert Comparison
records.description: CheXpert provides report-derived observation labels with uncertainty and a focused expert comparison. We do not use that dataset or claim to reproduce its multi-finding evaluation.

records.title: Comparing different deep learning architectures for classification of chest radiographs
records.description: The authors compared sixteen architectures on CheXpert and a separate COVID-19 collection. Comparable shallower models motivate measuring resource costs; their dataset-specific scores are not our results.

records.title: CheXtransfer: Performance and Parameter Efficiency of ImageNet Models for Chest X-Ray Interpretation
records.description: The study evaluates transfer and truncation on CheXpert, reporting an average parameter-efficiency improvement without a statistically significant drop in its comparison. That does not prove equivalence; our fine-tuning control does not reproduce truncation.

records.title: MedMNIST v2 - A large-scale lightweight benchmark for 2D and 3D biomedical image classification
records.description: The 2023 paper describes the standardized MedMNIST v2 collection at 28-pixel resolution. Our actual 224-pixel MedMNIST+ file is identified separately by its release record and checksum, rather than being an upscaled copy of the paper's 28-pixel images.
